_comment: ITS PURPOSE WAS TO MAKE THE PARITY QUESTIONS MEASURABLE AGAIN, not to
answer them. Both renderer arms were down when it started: the Electron
arm had no `src/build-debug-repro/bin/ct` at all, and the GPUI binary was
stale. This pass rebuilt the GPUI arm, cleared its freshness gate and ran
its capture lane end to end — so PARITY-G1 is re-measured here. The
Electron arm now LINKS, which it did not before, but its build still
cannot complete, so its lane could not run and PARITY-S1 and PARITY-P1
are NOT re-measured. They are recorded below as not measured rather than
inherited with a fresh date, which is the failure this campaign keeps
ONE FINDING OF THIS PASS IS ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT, NOT THE RENDERERS:
`ci/lib/build-freshness.sh` computes a DIFFERENT input digest outside the
dev shell than inside it, and reports a false STALE outside. See
supersedes: plat37-parity-readings-2026-10-14.json — for PARITY-G1 AND PARITY-S1. G1 was re-measured in this file's FIRST pass (2026-10-16 morning); S1 is re-measured in its SECOND pass (2026-10-16 afternoon, recorded under `secondPass`), on a real captured Electron frame, and the 2026-10-14 prediction that the census would drop to 5 is REFUTED — see regrade[PARITY-S1]. Every OTHER finding in the 2026-10-14 file and in plat37-parity-readings-2026-10-13.json stands unamended; neither pass re-measured them. PARITY-P1 is still NOT measured as a cross-renderer figure, and the second pass establishes WHY with a specific, newly-known cause: see regrade[PARITY-P1].
standing: HOST-CONDITIONAL EVIDENCE, NEVER A REQUIRED GATE. The GPUI window lane needs a live macOS GUI session and a kTCCServiceScreenCapture grant held by com.metacraft-labs.guiassert.capture. Neither exists on a fresh host or in CI.

gpuiArm.note: Built TWICE. The first build (11:38) emitted `WARNING: isonim-gpui's Rust shim is not built`, and because `isonim_gpui/bindings.nim` resolves the shim path with a COMPILE-TIME `when fileExists(...)`, that binary baked the bare leaf name `libgpui_nim_shim.dylib` and every lane run died with `could not load: libgpui_nim_shim.dylib`. Building the shims first (`cd isonim-gpui && nix develop --command just plat37-shims`, exit 0) and rebuilding made the lane work. THE BUILD ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING and is not expressed as a dependency anywhere.
gpuiArm.gateDigestUnchangedAcrossThatFix: 379c6803 both times, while the artefact sha moved d1d1cf78b1ec -> 95ad3d27cd17. The freshness closure therefore does NOT cover shim presence: two materially different binaries share one input digest.

electronArm.theLcryptoQuestionIsAnswered: RESOLVED, and the hypothesis in the brief is CONFIRMED. codetracer's dev shell itself populates LIBRARY_PATH with all five libraries the native link asks for. Measured under `nix develop`, with a positive control (the probe printed its own POSITIVE-CONTROL line) and a negative control (`libZZQQnonsense: NOT-FOUND`): LIBRARY_PATH length 361, carrying openssl-3.6.2/lib (libssl, libcrypto), sqlite-3.50.4/lib (libsqlite3), pcre-8.45/lib (libpcre), libzip-1.11.4/lib (libzip), zstd-1.5.7/lib (libzstd). `scripts/build-once.sh:400` independently derives the same set through `nix build --print-out-paths nixpkgs#openssl.out nixpkgs#sqlite.out nixpkgs#pcre.out nixpkgs#libzip.out nixpkgs#zstd.dev nixpkgs#zstd.out nixpkgs#clingo`. The earlier failure came from invoking `repro build ct-binary` DIRECTLY, which bypasses both. No store path was hardcoded.
electronArm.whereItStops: `nim c` with debug info on macOS shells out to a BARE `dsymutil` after the link. The `ctNative` edge became hermetic in codetracer 01d8b6e54 (2026-10-15 16:37) and declares only `clang` and `zstd-dev`, so the composed PATH has no `dsymutil` and the action dies with `sh: line 1: dsymutil: command not found` AFTER writing a working binary. `src/build-debug-repro/bin/ct.dSYM` is empty, consistent with this never having succeeded since that commit. At least TWO edges are affected: `ct` and `db-backend-record`.
electronArm.whyThatBlocksTheMeasurement: `scripts/build-once.sh:508` writes the Electron freshness stamp only after `repro build` returns 0. It never runs, so the stamp still describes an older artefact (stamp 17793057…, on disk 7ddad09b…), `build-freshness.sh electron-assert` exits 1, and `ci/test/plat37-macos-electron-capture.sh` refuses to capture through it BY DESIGN. The gate was not weakened, bypassed or hand-edited.
electronArm.fixAttemptedAndReverted: A `dsymutil` interface package (nixPackage "nixpkgs#llvm", executablePath "bin/dsymutil" — verified: nixpkgs#llvm resolves to llvm-21.1.8 whose bin/dsymutil is present, negative control bin/zzqq absent) plus adding "dsymutil" to the edge's tool identity refs did NOT clear the failure: both `ct` and `db-backend-record` still reported `dsymutil: command not found`. Both edits were REVERTED rather than left in the tree, because an unverified partial fix in a tracked file is worse than a clean tree plus this record. The real fix needs to cover every affected edge and belongs to the owner.

twoOtherBlockersClearedOnTheWay.shellcheckCatalog: The dev shell exports REPROBUILD_PACKAGES_ROOT to a flake-pinned catalog carrying only four interfaces (busybox, llvm, patchelf, sqlite3) and no `shellcheck`, which codetracer/repro.nim:564 `uses:`. Pointing REPROBUILD_PACKAGES_ROOT at the workspace sibling reprobuild-packages @ 9f981af6c7, which HAS packages/interfaces/shellcheck, cleared it — one of the three remedies the error message itself names.
twoOtherBlockersClearedOnTheWay.envelopeVersionMismatch: With the 2026-10-14 engine the build died with `repro interface extract: error: unsupported interface envelope version`. Cause, established by date rather than guess: `EnvelopeVersion` in libs/repro_interface_artifacts was bumped 27 -> 28 in reprobuild e5a62bf143 (2026-10-15 17:21), AFTER build/bin/reprobuild was compiled (2026-10-14 13:47). The `extract_runner` is compiled from the CURRENT checkout sources and so writes a v28 envelope that the older engine refuses. Rebuilding repro from the checkout cleared it. This is the stale-local-build hazard AGENTS.md documents, observed in the wild.

regrade.previousVerdict: REPRODUCES — 'the clamp reproduces and is measured, not read' (2026-10-13, at codetracer df80efc8d, on a rebuilt and gated GPUI binary).
regrade.verdict: REPRODUCES, re-measured on a fresh build at codetracer 6b6d05a081. GPUI still cannot reach the `wide` viewport on this display.
regrade.deficientSide: SEE belowWhichReportMatchesThePhysicalWindow — this pass declines to call GPUI the deficient side, and the previous files' framing is the thing most in need of revisiting.
regrade.reading: All 7 scenarios captured, 0 refused, every record carrying satisfiesG1: true. The split is exactly by viewport. The three `wide` scenarios (shell, editor, eventLog) each asked 1920x1080 points, got a 1728x1084-point window — `viewportHonoured: false`, `viewportDeviationPoints` {width: -192, height: -25} — and captured 3456x2168 device px. The four `laptop` scenarios (state, calltrace, editorWithMark, gutterLanes) each asked 1440x900 points, got 1440x929 points — `viewportHonoured: true`, deviation {0, 0} — and captured 2880x1858 device px. Read off the lane's own *.capture.json records, not off a picture and not off the console summary.
regrade.theGeometryIsSelfConsistent: The honoured case is the control for the clamped one. At `laptop` the window is 29 points TALLER than requested (929 vs 900) with deviation recorded as {0,0}, i.e. the 29-point title bar sits outside the content box. 929 - 29 = 900 exactly, and 2880x1858 device px minus the 58-px title bar is 2880x1800 — the extent the FLIP comparison has always run at. The same 29 points explain the clamped height deviation: 1084 - 29 = 1055, and 1080 - 1055 = 25, the recorded -25. The 58-device-px crop constant in build/plat37-parity/compare.sh is therefore confirmed by this pass, independently of any FLIP number.
regrade.whichReportMatchesThePhysicalWindow: This display is 1728x1117 points. GPUI's `wide` window is 1728x1084 points, which FITS it; a 1920-point-wide window does not exist on a 1728-point display. So GPUI's report is the physically realisable one. The counterpart measurement — what Electron reports for the same request, and whether its 1920x1080 is a logical framebuffer rather than a window — COULD NOT BE TAKEN this pass, because the Electron lane did not run. Until it is, the attribution of a 'deficient side' for G1 should be treated as open, not as settled by the earlier files.
regrade.consequenceForPixelComparison: Unchanged and now re-confirmed on fresh frames: 3 of the 7 captured scenarios sit at an extent no Electron frame can be compared against without resampling, and compare.sh refuses to resample. Only the 4 `laptop` scenarios are candidates for a pixel comparison.

regrade.verdict: REINSTATED. The Electron pane census does NOT come out at 5 — it is 7. Measured 2026-10-16 (second pass) on real captured frames from the freshly built, freshly stamped bundle at codetracer 6b6d05a081.
regrade.theOracleIsDerivedNotLiteral: The lane computes the expectation from the layout rather than hardcoding it: `_shared_default_visible_panes` over src/frontend/headless_app/shared_default_layout.generated.json evaluates to exactly ['calltrace','editor','eventLog','fileTree','state'] — 5 panes. That matched the brief's stated oracle exactly.
regrade.whatTheFramesActuallyShow: saw ['calltrace','editor','eventLog','fileTree','other','other','state'] — 7 drawn, 5 expected, extra ['other'] twice. Identical census on every one of the five refused scenarios (state, calltrace, eventLog, editorWithMark and one more), which is consistent with a layout-level cause rather than a per-scenario one.
regrade.soThe20261014PredictionIsRefuted: The 2026-10-14 fix set `noUserLayout` and the implied prediction was that the census would drop from 7 to 5. It did not. The two extra panes are classified `other`, i.e. they are panes the shared default layout does not place at all — so this is not a counting disagreement, it is two panes that should not be on the frame.
regrade.howTheLaneTreatsIt: Correctly, and consequentially: it REFUSES to write a reference .png for a frame whose census disagrees, on the stated grounds that such a frame is not a reference frame for parity. That refusal is what makes this finding block PARITY-P1 — see below.
regrade.control: Not a uniform-across-rows result in the vacuous sense: the geometry half of the same grading passed on all six scenarios ('honoured' for every one), and one scenario (shell) DID produce a graded frame. So the harness was capable of passing a frame and the census is what singled these out.

regrade.verdict: STILL NOT MEASURED as a cross-renderer figure — but this pass establishes the CAUSE, and the cause is PARITY-S1, not a missing Electron build.
regrade.whatChangedSinceTheFirstPass: The Electron arm now BUILDS and the lane now RUNS (it could not before). So the first pass's reason — 'no fresh Electron frames at all' — no longer applies. The new, narrower reason is below.
regrade.theBlockingFactMeasured: The Electron lane produced exactly ONE graded frame: `shell`. The other five were refused on the pane census (PARITY-S1), and a refused scenario gets NO reference .png written. `shell` is a `wide` scenario, and `wide` is precisely the class PARITY-G1 shows is dimensionally incomparable: compare.sh on it returns {"label":"shell","notComparable":"extent mismatch: gpui 3456x2168 (cropped 3456x2110) vs electron 3840x2160"}.
regrade.theExtentTableThatShowsTheTrap: gpui vs electron, device px, with GPUI's 58-px title-bar crop applied: shell 3456x2168->3456x2110 vs 3840x2160 MISMATCH; editor same MISMATCH; eventLog same MISMATCH; state 2880x1858->2880x1800 vs 2880x1800 MATCH; calltrace MATCH; editorWithMark MATCH. So the three scenarios that ARE comparable are exactly the three the census refused, and the one the lane graded is one of the three that are not.
regrade.whyNoNumberWasProducedAnyway: The three comparable views DO have Electron .png files on disk — but from 2026-10-12, four days and an unknown number of commits old. Comparing a fresh GPUI frame against those would reproduce the precise defect the build stamp exists to prevent (scripts/build-once.sh:485-500 records a published parity reading over artefacts '127 commits apart'). No such number was computed, and none should be.
regrade.theInstrumentWasVerIFIEDSOUNDThisPass: So that 'not measured' is not confused with 'instrument broken'. On the FRESH electron shell frame: identity comparison with itself gives mean 0.0, p50 0.0, p90 0.0, max 0.0, fracOver0_10 0.0; a 4-pixel self-shift of the same frame gives mean 0.06807, p50 0.0, p90 0.234431, max 0.983332, fracOver0_10 0.133547. Non-zero and non-uniform, so the tool discriminates.
regrade.statisticsAreAvailableWhenTheFigureCanBe: The first pass asked for mean/p50/p90/maxError beside fracOver0_10 because the thresholded fraction saturates. `flipdiff` ALREADY emits all of them (mean, p50, p90, p99, max, fracOver0_10, fracOver0_25, fracOver0_50) — no tooling change is needed, only a comparable fresh pair.
regrade.oneNoteOnTheSATURATIONLADDER: The brief's ladder (4 px -> 0.173) and this pass's 4-px self-shift on the shell frame (0.1335) differ. That is not a contradiction: the ladder is frame-dependent, being a function of how much high-frequency content the particular frame carries. It does mean the ladder should be quoted WITH the frame it was taken on.
regrade.readAlongsideNotApart: Unchanged from the standing analysis and not re-litigated here: when P1 is finally taken it belongs beside PARITY-S3 and PARITY-S5 (GPUI gives the editor essentially Electron's width, 352 vs 362, while making every other pane ~30% wider, with row pitch 25.8-26 against 24.3-25), because the distribution is bimodal (p50 ~0.0001, p90 ~0.68) and that is the signature of displaced structure rather than a global difference.

new.title: ci/lib/build-freshness.sh's GPUI half reports a FALSE STALE outside the dev shell, because it recomputes the input closure with whatever `nim` is on PATH (the Electron half is immune and must not be lumped in with it)
new.rootCauseFoundThisPass: ci/lib/build-freshness.sh:395-440 `bf_gpui_input_digest` does not read a recorded closure; it REGENERATES one by running `nim c --genDeps:on --compileOnly` (line 416) with the `nim` resolved from PATH (guarded only by a `command -v nim` existence check at line 400). `bf_deps_input_digest` (line 175-201) then folds every `/nix/store/...` line of the resulting `main.deps` into the digest as `store\t<path>`. The Nim standard-library modules in that listing live under the COMPILER'S OWN store path, so changing which nim is on PATH changes those lines and therefore the digest.
new.measured: Inside the codetracer dev shell the nim on PATH is /nix/store/2ry3sav2ghbn7a8xmcadvxksjgd94rhd-nim-fork-2.3.1-codetracer/bin/nim (Nim 2.3.1); outside it is a different compiler. Measured 2026-10-16 against codetracer 6b6d05a081: the previous pass recorded digest d7e6c03a... outside the shell on three consecutive runs (deterministic, not flaky) and 379c6803... inside it on the same tree at the same moment. The build stamps the inside-the-shell value, so the outside-the-shell verdict is a false STALE.
new.whyItMatters: The gate's whole purpose is to refuse a stale artefact. A false STALE is the opposite failure and it trains readers to disbelieve the gate. It also makes every gate reading un-interpretable unless the environment is stated, which is why every gate exit code in this file is recorded WITH its environment.
new.suggestedRemedy: Either (a) pin the compiler the digest is computed with — the stamp already records `built_by`, so the assertion could refuse when the nim on PATH is not that compiler, rather than silently digesting against a different one; or (b) exclude the compiler's own store subtree from the closure, so the digest describes the PROJECT's inputs rather than the toolchain's. (a) is the smaller change and keeps the closure honest; (b) risks dropping a real input. The existing `BF_BUILDER` note at lines 216-238 already works through exactly this class of error for `built_by`, so the file's own reasoning supports (a).
new.scopeCorrectedBySecondPass: The first pass wrote this up as a property of `build-freshness.sh`. Measured in the second pass, it is a property of the GPUI half ONLY. gpui: digest 379c6803… inside the dev shell vs d7e6c03a… outside, assert 0 inside and 1 outside. electron: digest 554173229a15d950… in BOTH environments and equal to the stamp, assert 0 in both. The difference is structural — `bf_electron_input_digest` digests git-tracked source content and never runs a compiler, while `bf_gpui_input_digest` shells out to `nim c --genDeps`.
new.additionalSuspectFoundThisPass: 'Inside vs outside the dev shell' may not be the real variable. scripts/build-once.sh:46 sources codetracer/.direnv/flake-profile-*.rc, dated 2026-08-27, which carries a DIFFERENT nim store path (y1cfnbf4…-nim-fork-2.3.1-codetracer) from the live dev shell's (2ry3sav2…-nim-fork-2.3.1-codetracer) — same version string, different store path, which is sufficient to move the digest. A third measurement arm (inside the shell, with the cached profile sourced) was NOT taken.

new.title: The gpui input closure does not cover the isonim-gpui Rust shim, so two materially different binaries share one digest
new.measured: Recorded by the previous pass and carried forward unamended (measured 2026-10-16 at codetracer 6b6d05a081): the GPUI binary was built twice. new.whyItMatters: A digest that is equal across two binaries that differ is not a freshness closure for those binaries. The gate would have passed a shim-less binary as fresh.

new.title: An unexpressed build order: the plat37 shims must exist before codetracer-gpui is compiled
new.detail: isonim_gpui/bindings.nim resolves the shim path with a COMPILE-TIME `when fileExists(...)`. The decision is therefore baked at compile time: if the Rust shim is not on disk when `codetracer-gpui` is compiled, the resulting binary is permanently shim-less and rebuilding the shim afterwards does not change it. Nothing in the graph expresses this ordering, so it holds only by the order a human happens to run two commands in.
new.whyItMatters: It is an ordering constraint enforced by nothing, and its violation is silent apart from one WARNING line — and, per FRESHNESS-CLOSURE-MISSES-SHIM, invisible to the freshness gate as well. The two defects compound: the order can be got wrong, and the gate cannot detect that it was.

new.title: Making the ctNative edge hermetic dropped `dsymutil`, so every macOS debug build of `ct` and `db-backend-record` has failed since codetracer 01d8b6e54
new.weCausedIt: codetracer 01d8b6e54 (2026-10-15 16:37) added `appendRegisteredActionToolIdentityRefs(ctNativeAction.id, [CtBackendCompiler, "zstd-dev"])` at repro.nim:972. Naming ANY tool ref opts the edge into a hermetic PATH (`actionPathDecision`, repro_cli_support.nim:1596-1750), so the edge stopped inheriting the ambient PATH on which it had been finding `dsymutil` by luck. The trade was correct — the ambient PATH was an undeclared input channel — but the declaration was incomplete.
new.failureShape: `nim c` with debugInfo on macOS shells out to a BARE `dsymutil` AFTER the link. The action therefore dies having ALREADY WRITTEN A WORKING BINARY: measured 2026-10-16, `src/build-debug-repro/bin/ct` was 11,389,600 bytes and `ct --version` printed `26.10.1(debug)`, while `ct.dSYM` held only an August artefact. 'The binary is there' must not be read as 'the edge succeeded'.
new.whyThePreviousAttemptFailed: The previous pass added a `dsymutil` package AND the tool-identity ref, and both edges still reported `dsymutil: command not found`. The missing third piece is that A TOOL REF IS INERT UNLESS THE RECIPE ALSO HAS A MATCHING `uses:` ENTRY — the resolver returns `none` for a name no `uses:` entry declares (repro_cli_support.nim:7686-7712; the rule is stated in the stdlib at packages/nim.nim:741-743). With no `uses: "dsymutil"` in codetracer/repro.nim the ref added no directory to the composed PATH, so the fix was a no-op by design rather than by accident. A bare `uses:` entry additionally only auto-resolves if the selector is registered in `BundledStdlibSelectors`.

freshnessGatesThisPass.theMechanism: `bf_gpui_input_digest` (ci/lib/build-freshness.sh:395-440) REGENERATES the closure by running `nim c --genDeps:on --compileOnly` with whatever `nim` is on PATH (guarded only by a `command -v nim` existence test at line 400), and `bf_deps_input_digest` folds every resulting `/nix/store/...` line in verbatim as `store\t<path>`. The Nim stdlib modules live under the COMPILER'S own store path, so a different nim means a different digest. `bf_electron_input_digest` (line 537) instead digests git-tracked source content (`git ls-files -s`, the worktree overlay, and untracked non-ignored files) and never invokes a compiler — which is exactly why it does not drift.
